subject: WatchHouse trial: instrumentation agenda, success criteria & owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@watchhouse.ai>, Eng Team <eng@watchhouse.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: WatchHouse trial: instrumentation agenda, success criteria & owners

Thanks again for taking the deep dive today — appreciate the clear product context. Per our call, I put together a concise plan for the 4-week trial so we can align on what success looks like and who owns what. Please review and flag anything obvious.

Key objectives (what WatchHouse wants to validate):
- End-to-end latency under typical load (p95 tail below 400ms) for the generate/chat flow
- Stable token cost within expected envelope (<= $0.003/token for the baseline model)
- No functional regressions vs your internal golden prompts (we'll run your 12 test prompts)
- Observability: ability to triage errors to root cause within 10 mins (logs + traces + request-id correlation)

Suggested instrumentation & dashboards for POC (we can stand these up on Day 1):
1) API health dashboard: 1m/5m request rate, 5xx rate, success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms)
2) Cost dashboard: tokens per request, per-route cost, cache hit ratio for prefix/KV caching
3) Tracing view: per-request span breakdown (frontend -> routing -> model inference -> post-processing), average inference GPU time
4) Errors & anomalies: top error messages, correlated prompts, sampling of failing inputs (redacted)
5) Throughput vs latency curve: synthetic ramp and real traffic overlay

Ownership (proposal):
- Redwood: Ben Carter (trial PM) — infrastructure, dashboards, runbooks, model/variant routing config
- WatchHouse: Samir (POC owner) & Eng Team (2 ICs named on-call) — provide golden prompts, expected traffic profile, procurement contact for any contract items

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (start): Kickoff + data handoff + share golden prompts (target: 2027-09-15)
- Week 1: Baseline deploy + basic dashboards + first smoke tests (2027-09-16 to 2027-09-22)
- Week 2: Instrumentation tuning + tracing enabled + run golden prompt suite (2027-09-23 to 2027-09-29)
- Week 3: Load ramp, cost analysis, mitigation iteration (2027-09-30 to 2027-10-06)
- Week 4: Final evaluation, exec recap, decision meeting (target: 2027-10-08)

Attachments: I attached a small success-criteria workbook and our observability template JSON for the dashboards.

Next steps for WatchHouse (please):
- Confirm owners for engineering (names + slack IDs)
- Share golden prompt set and expected request distribution (sample rates per route)
- Confirm any compliance constraints for log export (PII redaction rules)

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: WatchHouse trial: instrumentation agenda, success criteria & owners

Appreciate the quick confirmations. Short answers on the compliance ask:
- Field-level redaction: supported. We will provide a config file so you can specify fields to redact before logs leave your VPC.
- Storage encryption: logs are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS for Private customers; for hosted trials we use AES-256 and will set TTL-based retention per your policy.

I've attached the observability JSON template (example dashboards + metrics mapping) so your SREs can scan. On the kickoff I'll propose we allocate 90 minutes: 1) handoff + access, 2) baseline smoke run, 3) dashboard scope discussion, 4) procurement/contract quick sync.

Concrete asks from Redwood before kickoff:
- A sample of 50 redacted requests for our smoke tests (no PII)
- Your expected QPS and burst profile (sample csv)
- Procurement contact if we need an MSA amendment or temporary SLA for the trial

I'll also add suggested monitoring queries in the shared Drive folder.

— Ben
